comments.body:
Thanks for this, and for the clear write-up.

One thing doesn't match the default client. In `ollama` 0.6.x, `AbortableAsyncIterator` already throws `Did not receive done or success response in stream.` when the response ends without a `done` chunk. `doStream`'s `start()` catches that and calls `controller.error()`, so the stream errors, `streamText`'s `onError` already fires, and the new `flush()` never runs on that path. A cut connection also surfaces as a thrown fetch/body error, which takes the same route.

So the new `flush()` only matters for a custom `OllamaClient` adapter whose iterator ends cleanly without `done`. That's a valid case, since the client is injectable, but it's narrower than the description says.

Before we merge:
1. Update the description, the code comment and the changeset to say this is hardening for custom clients that end without `done`, not a fix for dropped connections with the default client.
2. Add a test for the path the default client actually takes: an iterator that yields a chunk and then throws. Check that the stream errors and that no synthetic `finish` part is added.

Happy to merge once those are in.

Thanks, you're right: with the default client, `ollama` 0.6.x's `AbortableAsyncIterator` already throws when the response ends without `done`, so `flush()` never runs there. I reworded the code comment and the PR description so this is presented as hardening for custom `OllamaClient` adapters whose iterator ends cleanly, and added a test for the default-client path (an iterator that yields a chunk and then throws errors the stream with no synthetic `finish`/`error` part). The change is in b23592a.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
